data.description:
## Description
**What**: Ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> that walks the epic subtree, reads all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments, and merges by stable intent_id using stage precedence (brainstorm < preplanning < implementation-plan), most-recent-timestamp within stage, and comment-UUID lexical order as the same-timestamp tiebreaker. Surfaces a _conflicts array for equal-stage duplicates and interleaved-stage anomalies, and preserves unknown fields.
**Why**: This is the read half of the walking skeleton; without a deterministic merge, every consumer and the validator would see raw, conflicting comment streams.
**Scope**:
- IN: subtree walk; stage-precedence merge; timestamp and UUID tiebreakers; _conflicts array (equal-stage duplicates + interleaved-stage anomalies); unknown-field passthrough.
- OUT: finding classification (sc-6); a03c hook (sc-7).

## Done Definitions

- intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> walks the epic subtree and returns one merged entry per stable intent_id across all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When the same intent_id appears at brainstorm and preplanning stages, the merged entry reflects the preplanning value, confirming stage precedence ← Satisfies: sc-5
- When two same-stage comments share a timestamp, the merge selects the entry whose comment UUID sorts first, producing identical output across repeated runs ← Satisfies: sc-5
- The _conflicts array lists equal-stage duplicates and interleaved-stage anomalies such as an implementation-plan timestamp predating a later preplanning write ← Satisfies: sc-5
- Unknown entry fields present in input comments appear unchanged in the merged output, and unit tests written and passing cover all merge, tiebreaker, and passthrough logic ← Satisfies: sc-5

## Considerations

- [Determinism] The comment-UUID lexical tiebreaker is the only defense against equal-timestamp non-determinism; it must be applied before output is emitted.
- [Clock-skew] Interleaved-stage anomalies from worktree clock skew are surfaced in _conflicts, not silently resolved.
- [Shell hygiene] intent-allocation-read.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit on creation.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a downstream consumer, I want intent-allocation-read.sh to merge all stage comments by stable intent_id with deterministic tiebreakers, so that I read one resolved manifest per epic.
